title: Deputy Attorney General Febrie Adriansyah Resigns Amid Corruption Raids
detail: Febrie Adriansyah, Indonesia's Deputy Attorney General for Special Crimes and the country's top anti-corruption prosecutor, resigned after police raided 12 locations on July 8–9, seizing Rp476 billion (~$29 million), 74kg of gold bullion, and millions in US and Singapore dollars — including from a Sentul, Bogor property Adriansyah later acknowledged was his. Police named him a suspect in the 'Sumatra Blackout' probe into coal-supply procurement corruption for state power plants between 2018 and 2026, tied to recent grid blackouts. Attorney General ST Burhanuddin accepted the resignation to preserve the integrity of the investigation. TNI soldiers were seen guarding Adriansyah's residence during the raids, exposing friction between the police, the Attorney General's Office, and the military.

media.caption: Indonesia's top anti-corruption prosecutor Febrie Adriansyah resigns amid Sumatra Blackout graft probe
